findings.title: Crash recovery terminalizes an unverifiable non-reversible mutation and re-arms response
findings.evidence: Intent-only terminate_process recovery writes a terminal failure but does not trip the mutation circuit; inert reconciliation returned true with mutation_blocked false and no recovery_required state.
findings.impact: A crash-interrupted non-reversible host mutation is discarded from manual-review state and later elevated mutations are re-authorized.
findings.recommendation: Keep non-reversible orphan intents recovery-required, open the mutation circuit, and require authenticated operator disposition before re-arming.

closure.summary: Fourth reopened residual closed: recovery authorization now issues an OS-protected, host-bound, monotonically sequenced one-process challenge for the exact latest mutation-started ORPHAN. Its resource cryptographically binds the install epoch, challenge counter/nonce, action/combat/generation, selected allowlisted disposition, and full normalized-reason digest. Resolution uses a monotonic deadline rather than reversible wall time, durably consumes the challenge, and retains the complete HMAC-verifiable human AuthorizationDecision. Ordered replay requires the exact terminal schema, action/combat/status/disposition/reason, orphan and challenge bindings, and policy receipt; malformed HMAC-authentic terminals remain non-terminal. The protected anchor tracks the latest journal sequence/HMAC, so journal rollback or deletion stays health 0 and disarmed. Whole-host rollback including the journal key and protected store remains outside software-only proof.

findings.title: The response journal has quadratic append cost and silently ignores old live actions
findings.evidence: Every append rereads and re-verifies the full unbounded journal; startup and undo operations return only the latest 500 or 5000 actions.
findings.impact: Incident volume can exhaust response resources and older active mutations can disappear from runtime state or undo-all semantics.
findings.recommendation: Add authenticated segmentation/checkpoints, quotas, compaction, a complete live-action index, and fail-safe exhaustion health.

findings.title: Quarantine moves one hard-link name while an executable alias remains live
findings.evidence: POSIX and Windows pinned-file paths do not reject link count greater than one; an inert two-link rename left the alternate alias readable after quarantine.
findings.impact: The module can commit successful quarantine while the same malicious file object remains executable by another name.
findings.recommendation: Require and receipt-bind link count one, revalidate on the pinned handle, and fail closed when alias-safe quarantine cannot be proved.

findings.title: Model attestation silently re-enrolls lost state, missing files, and new content
findings.evidence: Malformed baseline becomes empty TOFU; missing baseline entries are not checked; new/error values auto-pin; AI Triage verifies a tag name but not an attested manifest digest.
findings.impact: Poisoned, missing, unreadable, or silently re-enrolled model content can be reported clean and used for triage.
findings.recommendation: Use an authenticated atomic complete inventory, fail non-clean on missing/new/error entries, and gate exact-tag inference on a fresh attestation receipt.

findings.title: API Patch Detector reports zero checked exports as 100% clean and caches failure forever
findings.evidence: Baseline exceptions cache an empty map permanently; zero comparisons produce no findings and the run loop sets health 100 with zero exports clean.
findings.impact: Anti-blinding coverage can be absent for the process lifetime while health remains green.
findings.recommendation: Require the complete fixed export set, retry baseline failure, expose per-export coverage, and never score zero/partial comparison as clean.

findings.title: ARP Watchdog trusts startup/new poison and treats collector failure as healthy
findings.evidence: ARP command failure becomes an empty successful result; run and self-test accept it; every first-seen mapping is trusted in volatile memory.
findings.impact: Pre-start/restart/new-address ARP poisoning and collector loss can be blessed as a healthy baseline.
findings.recommendation: Persist authenticated adapter-scoped state, require independent enrollment evidence, and separate collector completeness from valid empty data.

findings.title: AV Telemetry Bridge deliberately discards retained detections and has no restart-safe cursor
findings.evidence: Startup drains all retained events without processing, fallback seeds all existing threats, recurring failures are swallowed, and no bookmark/generation/gap state exists.
findings.impact: Restart or collector failure creates invisible Defender telemetry gaps for downstream consumers.
findings.recommendation: Use authenticated WEVT bookmarks and generation anchors, retained replay, explicit gap events, and failure-aware health.

findings.title: Connection-based detectors fail open; the inference-port allowlist is basename-only
findings.evidence: Both modules return silently on shared connection-snapshot exceptions and then report 100; Counter-Agentic exempts generic mutable process names.
findings.impact: Socket visibility can disappear silently and a renamed client can evade local inference-port detection.
findings.recommendation: Propagate typed snapshot completeness into health and bind allowed clients to process birth plus object-resolved signed/digested executable identity.

findings.title: Canary Drill can reach 100% without testing the promised durable recorder path
findings.evidence: The contract promises FlightRecorder verification, but health is calculated solely from in-memory EventBus echoes and the file has no ledger query/receipt path.
findings.impact: Forensic persistence may be broken while the canary pipeline reports complete health.
findings.recommendation: Require a second authenticated recorder receipt for the exact canary and score live echo and durable persistence independently.

findings.title: Continuous Chaos Harness satisfies every probe with its own announcement
findings.evidence: Broad module/message keyword predicates match the harness's own APID, entropy DNS, and EICAR FIM/AMSI announcement; inert fake-bus checks returned true for all three without detector events.
findings.impact: All tested sensors can be absent while the assurance control reports every detector responsive and health 100.
findings.recommendation: Use nonce-bound strict responder receipts from allowlisted module identities and reject self/practice/text-only echoes.

closure.summary: Reopened residual closed: a manager-held broker enrolls exact built-in detector objects and gives each a detector-specific object capability and private per-enrollment MAC authority. Receipts bind capability ID, module/code, lifecycle generation, source epoch, one-time nonce/challenge, exact observed-target digest, observation, and time. Generic publishers with the shared EventBus and every public field cannot mint a valid receipt. APID, FIM, and enabled native AMSI issue receipts only after real object-bound observations; NDRD's shared-bus DNS source intentionally remains unassured rather than self-satisfying.

findings.title: Compliance artifact calls mappings enforced and hides bounded-bus loss
findings.evidence: Detection mappings are emitted as nist_control_enforced/stig_baseline_enforced; bus overflow is ignored, only 2000 volatile incidents remain, and health stays 100.
findings.impact: A partial relevance crosswalk can be mistaken for complete evidence that controls are implemented and effective.
findings.recommendation: Separate mapping from implementation/assessment evidence and persist authenticated coverage, gaps, truncation, and exact report scope.

findings.title: Daily briefing is an unbounded-age last-500 sample and reports success before persistence
findings.evidence: Recent 500 events are not filtered to a daily interval; count/ready emission precede file writes and all write failures are swallowed.
findings.impact: Busy-day events may be omitted, stale events included, or no durable report produced while health reports success.
findings.recommendation: Use a durable closed interval with gaps/counts and emit success only after validated atomic persistence.

findings.title: Deception detects writes/deletes, not the credential reads it promises to trap
findings.evidence: File traps poll only modification time and registry trap code only writes a value; no read observer exists. Inert read left mtime unchanged.
findings.impact: Credential thieves can read decoy files/registry values without alerting or producing a SOAR recommendation.
findings.recommendation: Use OS-native audited read telemetry bound to exact file/registry identities and degrade health when read visibility is unavailable.

findings.title: Driver provenance describes mutable path samples, not one pinned loaded image
findings.evidence: Hash and Authenticode are separate path operations guarded only by size/mtime, with no file handle/object/link identity or binding to loaded kernel image bytes.
findings.impact: A privileged attacker can compose benign provenance for a different or replaced loaded driver image.
findings.recommendation: Pin the exact image object, bind hash/signature/catalog and loaded-module identity, and label unbound path samples unknown.

findings.title: eBPF telemetry can be name-filtered away and loses events without accounting
findings.evidence: Every exec whose current comm begins sys is dropped; perf buffers have no lost callback, callbacks swallow errors, IPv6 identity is omitted, and successful poll restores health 100.
findings.impact: An attacker-selected name or buffer pressure can erase Linux telemetry invisibly.
findings.recommendation: Remove basename drops, add loss/error/sequence accounting and IPv6 evidence, and derive health from measured delivery completeness.

findings.title: Security-log reader skips event bursts and never recovers from channel generation reset
findings.evidence: Only one newest backward batch is read before the cursor advances; startup drops history and record-number reset leaves every new record below the sticky cursor while health stays 100.
findings.impact: Event flooding or clear/refill can hide process/logon telemetry from a core sensor without a health signal.
findings.recommendation: Use authenticated WEVT bookmarks/generation anchors and bounded forward pagination without advancing past unread evidence.

closure.summary: Fourth reopened residual closed: cursor v3 and high-water v2 are now witnessed by a separately stored OS-protected, host-bound rollback anchor carrying an install epoch, monotonic challenge counter, current cursor/high-water HMACs, and consumed request state. Deleting both local state files or restoring an older valid pair cannot recreate/reuse an approval or restore green health; a fresh random anchor challenge and distinct human approval are required. Enrollment uses a process-monotonic deadline and binds the install epoch, challenge nonce/counter, exact gap/generation/cursor/bounds/reason, and a bounded digest of every retained record. The live channel identity is serialized and resampled before and after the durable cursor/high-water/anchor commit; any pre-bookmark replacement persists a gap and replays degraded. Missing/unverifiable external anchor authority explicitly caps health. Whole-host rollback including the protected store/signing authority and telemetry snapshot remains outside software-only proof.

findings.title: Real-time ETW health is a sticky local boolean, not session liveness or delivery
findings.evidence: Only stop clears running; asynchronous consumer termination and callback errors do not, and no loss/heartbeat metric exists. Wrapper health checks only that boolean.
findings.impact: A dead, stalled, or lossy ETW session can continue to report live at health 100.
findings.recommendation: Supervise the real session/thread, consume error/loss callbacks, require bounded liveness proof, and restart or remain degraded.
